item.title: PHP usort Multiple Criteria Sorting Strategies
item.description:
“PHP usort Multiple Criteria Sorting Strategies”

When dealing with arrays of objects or associative arrays in PHP, organizing the data based on specific properties or keys is a common requirement. The usort() function provides a powerful way to achieve custom sorting by allowing you to define your own comparison logic. This question explores various effective strategies for sorting PHP arrays based on one or multiple criteria.

Sorting by a Single Object Property

A primary use case is sorting an array of objects by a particular property. For instance, if you have an array of user objects and want to sort them alphabetically by their name property, usort() is an excellent choice.

item.title: Top 15 Ways to Sort Multi-Dimensional Arrays in PHP
item.description:
“Top 15 Ways to Sort Multi-Dimensional Arrays in PHP”

Sorting multi-dimensional arrays is a fundamental task in PHP development. Whether you need to order data by a specific key, handle multiple sorting criteria, or maintain key associations, PHP offers a variety of powerful functions. This guide delves into numerous techniques, providing clear explanations and practical code examples to help you master array sorting.

Solution 1: Using usort with Custom Comparison Functions

The usort function is a versatile tool for sorting arrays by values using a user-defined comparison function. This is particularly useful for multi-dimensional arrays where you need to define the sorting logic explicitly.
